Get some rest. Before you go, I made one mistake in the A natural minor left hand. I labeled **C₃ – E₃ – A₃** as "C/E," but that's actually **Am in first inversion** (Am/C). A real **C/E** is **E₃ – G₃ – C₄**. Either works to support A minor. Am/C is probably the better choice for reinforcing A as home, since it still contains the A.

Also, in the C natural minor version, it's really the Eb and Ab that make it sound minor, not the D and Bb in the descent.

Everything else should play as written. Good luck with the motif, and sleep well!

- To fit 10 notes, the melodic lines (3, 6, 7c) don't repeat the original C E G A G E shape exactly. They keep the opening and the raised notes, then descend and land on the tonic.

If you want a fully stepwise descent in the melodic versions, you'd need a few more notes than the 10-note limit allows.
